trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Lisbon, Portugal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour
experiences.description: Spend a culinary afternoon at the iconic Time Out Market sampling the best of Portuguese cuisine including bacalhau (salt cod), pastéis de nata, piri piri chicken, and local cheeses, all curated from top Lisbon chefs under one roof alongside the historic Mercado da Ribeira.

experiences.name: Belém Historical Landmarks & Pastéis de Belém
experiences.description: Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery and the iconic Tower of Belém, both masterpieces of Manueline architecture dating to the Age of Discovery. Finish with a visit to the original Pastéis de Belém bakery, open since 1837, for the world-famous custard tarts straight from the oven.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use the time to collect luggage, clear customs, and take the Metro (Linha Vermelha/Red Line) from Aeroporto station to the city center. Affordable and direct, costing around €1.50 with a reloadable Viva Viagem card.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Lisbon City Stay and freshen up. Once settled, take a leisurely walk through the Baixa-Chiado neighborhood to get your bearings. Stroll through Praça do Comércio (Commerce Square) along the Tagus River — free to visit and one of Lisbon's most iconic squares. Walk up to Rua Augusta for a feel of the city's buzzing street life.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Alfama district, Lisbon's oldest neighborhood. Explore the winding cobblestone streets as the sun sets and soak in the atmosphere. Find a miradouro (viewpoint) such as Portas do Sol for panoramic views over the city and river at no cost.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastel de nata (custard tart, ~€1.20) and a bica (espresso, ~€0.80) at a local café near the airport or in Baixa upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a light snack such as a prego (steak sandwich) from a local tasca in Baixa for around €4–6.
meals.dinner: Dine at a traditional tasca in Alfama. Look for a prato do dia (daily special) which typically includes soup, main course, bread, and a drink for €8–12. Try dishes like bacalhau à brás (codfish) or caldo verde soup.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 24-hour or rechargeable Viva Viagem card at the airport Metro station (€0.50 card fee + credit). This covers Metro, bus, and tram rides. Keep valuables secure in Alfama as it can be touristy and pickpocketing occurs.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a visit to the Castelo de São Jorge (St. George's Castle). Arrive early to beat the crowds. Entry is €15 for adults but offers stunning panoramic views of Lisbon and the Tagus River. Explore the Moorish ramparts, towers, and the small archaeological museum inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill through the Alfama district and explore its labyrinthine streets, tiled building facades (azulejos), and local life. Visit the Museu do Azulejo (National Tile Museum) — entry is €5 — to learn about Portugal's iconic decorative tile tradition, a must-see for history lovers.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a free or low-cost Fado moment: many tascas in Alfama offer live Fado music during dinner. Head to a local restaurant that includes Fado with your meal. Alternatively, wander to Largo do Intendente for a more local, less touristy evening vibe.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a neighborhood padaria (bakery) near your hotel for a torrada (toast with butter) and coffee for around €2–3.
meals.lunch: Eat at a simple café near the Museu do Azulejo or pack a picnic from a local mini-market — grab local cheese, bread, and fruit for under €5.
meals.dinner: Find a tasca in Alfama offering Fado nights with dinner. Budget around €12–18 for a full meal including soup, main, and a glass of wine. Ask locals for recommendations to avoid tourist-trap pricing.

day_by_day.notes: The Museu do Azulejo is slightly outside the center but easily reachable by bus (28E tram or bus 794). Wear comfortable shoes — Alfama's hills and cobblestones are tough on feet. Carry a light jacket for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Take the iconic Tram 28E (€3 with Viva Viagem card) from Martim Moniz through Alfama, Graça, and up to Campo de Ourique. This is one of Lisbon's most scenic and historic tram rides. Alternatively, walk up to the Miradouro da Graça for one of the best free viewpoints in the city, especially beautiful in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Book the Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour experience. Spend a culinary afternoon at the iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré sampling the best of Portuguese cuisine. Even without a formal tour, you can explore the market independently — try petiscos (Portuguese tapas), fresh seafood, and local wines. Budget around €15–20 for a self-guided tasting session.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the LX Factory, a creative hub in a repurposed industrial complex in Alcântara (especially lively on Sundays with a market). Browse local artisan stalls, enjoy street food, and soak in Lisbon's creative culture. Entry is free.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a classic Lisbon breakfast at a café near your hotel — galão (milky coffee) and a croissant or pastel de nata for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Time Out Market — try a bifana (pork sandwich), grilled sardines, or a selection of petiscos. Budget €10–15 for a satisfying lunch.
meals.dinner: Grab street food or a snack at LX Factory on Sunday evening — options include burgers, crepes, and local bites for €5–10. Or head back to Baixa for a budget prato do dia at a local restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: Tram 28E can get very crowded on weekends — go early or be prepared to wait. LX Factory's Sunday market runs until around 19:00–20:00. Time Out Market is open daily and does not require advance booking for self-guided visits.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train from Cais do Sodré station to Belém (approx. 15–20 min, ~€1.50 each way). Begin the Belém Historical Landmarks experience: visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a stunning example of Manueline architecture. Entry is €10, or free on the first Sunday of the month. Spend at least 1.5 hours exploring the cloisters and church.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Belém with the iconic Torre de Belém (Tower of Belém), another UNESCO-listed Manueline masterpiece on the Tagus riverbank. Entry is €6. Afterwards, walk along the riverside promenade and visit the Padrão dos Descobrimentos (Monument to the Discoveries) — exterior viewing is free, or pay €6 to go inside. Don't miss the famous Pastéis de Belém bakery (the original since 1837) — try the warm custard tarts with cinnamon for just €1.30 each.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon and explore the Chiado neighborhood. Visit the historic Livraria Bertrand (world's oldest operating bookshop, free entry) and browse the elegant streets. Relax at Praça de Camões or a nearby café.

meals.breakfast: Eat near your hotel before departing for Belém — coffee and toast at a local café for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Have lunch in Belém at a local café or bring a picnic. Alternatively, try a simple restaurant near the monastery for a prato do dia at €9–12.
meals.dinner: Dine in Chiado or Bairro Alto — both neighborhoods have a range of budget-friendly tascas. Try arroz de marisco (seafood rice) or grilled fish for €10–14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Belém is best explored as a half-day or full-day trip. Start early to beat tour groups at the Monastery. Combine Jerónimos and Torre de Belém visits with a combo ticket if available (~€12). The Pastéis de Belém queue can be long but moves quickly — it's absolutely worth the wait.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga (National Museum of Ancient Art) in Santos, one of Portugal's most important art museums. Entry is €6. Explore Portuguese paintings, decorative arts, and historical artifacts spanning several centuries — a wonderful blend of history and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mouraria neighborhood, Lisbon's oldest Moorish quarter and the birthplace of Fado. Wander through Largo do Intendente Pina Manique, a beautifully restored square. Visit the free Museu do Fado (exterior and courtyard) or pay €5 for the full exhibition to learn about Fado's history and cultural significance. End with a walk through Martim Moniz square, a multicultural hub with cheap food stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your final evening at a rooftop bar or miradouro for sunset views. Miradouro da Senhora do Monte is the highest viewpoint in Lisbon and completely free. Afterwards, have a farewell dinner in the Bairro Alto or Príncipe Real area, sampling classic Portuguese dishes one last time.

meals.breakfast: Visit a local mercearia (grocery/deli) or padaria near the hotel for a final traditional Lisbon breakfast — coffee, pastel de nata, and fresh orange juice for €3–4.
meals.lunch: Eat at the multicultural food stalls around Martim Moniz — try a prato do dia or street food from one of the affordable vendors for €5–8.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a Bairro Alto tasca. Order caldo verde (kale soup), grilled bacalhau (salted cod), and a glass of vinho verde (green wine) — full meal for €12–16. Toast to a wonderful Lisbon trip!

day_by_day.notes: If your return flight is on May 20th or later, use this evening to pack and prepare. Lisbon Airport is accessible via the Red Metro line from downtown in about 25–30 minutes for €1.50. Keep your Viva Viagem card topped up for the journey back. Total estimated daily budget (excluding accommodation): €30–50 per day covering transport, entry fees, and meals.

trip_options.title: Classic Lisbon, Portugal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line to Green Line) to your hotel, Lisbon City Stay. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a short walk around your neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Baixa-Chiado, Lisbon's elegant downtown grid. Visit Praça do Comércio by the Tagus riverfront, walk up to Chiado for window shopping, and soak in the city's first impressions at a relaxed pace. Stop at Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara for a panoramic view over the city.
day_by_day.evening: Alfama District Walking Tour & Fado Show — join an early-evening guided walk through Lisbon's oldest medieval neighborhood, winding through cobbled alleys, past tiled facades and ancient churches. Cap the night with a live Fado performance at a traditional casa de fado, experiencing Portugal's soul music firsthand.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastel de nata and a galão (milky espresso) at a café near the airport or upon arrival at a local pastelaria in Baixa.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick but authentic bite at Tasca do Chico or a local tascas (tavern) in Chiado — try a bifana (pork sandwich) or a prato do dia (daily special) for €10–14.
meals.dinner: Dinner is included as part of the Fado show experience at a traditional Alfama restaurant. Expect grilled fish, petiscos (Portuguese tapas), and house wine — budget €35–50 per person with the show.

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 13:00, so nothing is scheduled before check-in. Book the Fado show in advance as evening slots fill up quickly, especially on weekends. Wear comfortable walking shoes — Alfama's hills and cobblestones can be challenging.

day_by_day.morning: LX Factory Sunday Market & Local Dining — head to LX Factory in the Alcântara district for its famous weekly Sunday market. Browse stalls selling vintage goods, local crafts, artisan foods, books, and design pieces inside a beautifully repurposed 19th-century industrial complex. Arrive by 10:00 to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour — make your way to the iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré (a short walk or tram ride from LX Factory). Spend the afternoon sampling the best of Portuguese cuisine: from grilled octopus and bacalhau (salt cod) dishes to artisan cheeses, ginjinha (cherry liqueur), and pastéis de nata. A curated culinary journey through multiple vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Wander along the Ribeira waterfront promenade as the sun sets over the Tagus. Settle into a relaxed riverside bar or miradouro for sundowner drinks — try a glass of vinho verde or a local craft beer. End the evening with a quiet dinner in the Cais do Sodré or Santos neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Start at LX Factory's own café, Landeau Chocolate or the in-house bakery — try a freshly baked croissant and specialty coffee (€5–8).
meals.lunch: Graze through Time Out Market stalls — budget €15–25 per person for a satisfying multi-dish tasting lunch from award-winning chefs and local producers.
meals.dinner: Dine at a local tasca in Santos or Cais do Sodré. Try Taberna da Rua das Flores or a similar mid-range spot for petiscos and grilled fish — €20–30 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: LX Factory's Sunday Market runs from approximately 10:00–19:00. Combine it naturally with Time Out Market in the afternoon since both are in the western riverside area, making logistics easy. Carry a small bag for market purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Belém Historical Landmarks & Pastéis de Belém — take Tram 15E or a rideshare to Belém (20–25 min from city center). Begin with the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking example of Manueline architecture built in the 16th century to celebrate Vasco da Gama's voyage to India. Explore the ornate cloisters and church interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Belém with a visit to the iconic Tower of Belém, standing sentinel on the Tagus riverbank — another Manueline masterpiece and UNESCO World Heritage Site. Also visit the Monument to the Discoveries (Padrão dos Descobrimentos) nearby. Then make the essential stop at the original Pastéis de Belém bakery (since 1837) for the world-famous custard tarts, warm from the oven, dusted with cinnamon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center and explore the Príncipe Real neighborhood — a charming, leafy quarter with antique shops, concept stores, and excellent restaurants. Enjoy a relaxed evening dinner in this upscale but approachable neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café near Lisbon City Stay — coffee and toast with butter and jam (€4–7).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Belém at Vela Latina or a riverside café — try grilled sardines or bacalhau à brás (shredded salt cod with eggs and potatoes) for €12–18.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Príncipe Real — try A Cevicheria (creative Portuguese-Peruvian fusion) or Taberna da Rua das Flores for traditional petiscos. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Jerónimos Monastery is closed on Mondays for free entry but remains open with a paid ticket (€10). Book tickets online in advance to skip queues. The Tower of Belém can have long lines — arrive early or pre-book. Belém is about 6 km west of the city center.

day_by_day.morning: Sintra Royal Palaces Day Trip — take the scenic 40-minute train from Rossio Station (trains run frequently, €2.30 each way) to the fairy-tale town of Sintra. Begin with the flamboyant Pena Palace, perched dramatically on a hilltop with colorful Romantic-era architecture and sweeping views over the Atlantic and surrounding forests. Explore the palace interior and terraces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore more of Sintra's magic: walk the forested paths to the Moorish Castle (Castelo dos Mouros) for medieval ramparts and panoramic views, or visit the mystical Quinta da Regaleira with its mysterious initiation wells and neo-Manueline architecture. Stroll through Sintra village for local pastries — try travesseiros (almond and egg cream pastries) at Piriquita bakery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lisbon by train in the late afternoon. Spend a gentle evening exploring the Mouraria neighborhood (next to Alfama), Lisbon's multicultural heart with excellent local restaurants, street art, and a relaxed local vibe. Enjoy a well-deserved rest after a full day trip.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel or grab a pastel de nata and coffee at Rossio Station café before boarding the train (€4–6).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Sintra village — try Tascantiga or a local restaurant for a prato do dia or grilled meat. Budget €12–18 per person. Alternatively, pack snacks to save time between palaces.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Mouraria back in Lisbon — try Zé da Mouraria or another neighborhood tasca for hearty traditional Portuguese cooking. Budget €18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Sintra is best explored on foot or by local bus (434/435 tuk-tuk shuttle between sites — €3–5). Wear sturdy walking shoes as paths are steep and uneven. Book Pena Palace tickets online in advance (€14) — it sells out, especially in spring. Start early to maximize time and avoid midday crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a leisurely final morning revisiting your favorite Lisbon neighborhood or exploring something missed — consider the Museu Nacional do Azulejo (National Tile Museum) to discover the history of Portugal's iconic azulejo tiles, housed in a stunning 16th-century convent in the Beato district (€5 entry). A perfect, compact morning museum visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city center for last-minute exploration: ride the iconic Tram 28E through Alfama and Graça for a scenic tour of Lisbon's hills (€3, a local institution). Stop at Miradouro da Graça or Miradouro da Senhora do Monte for the best panoramic views in the city. Pick up souvenirs — local ceramics, tinned fish, ginjinha, or cork goods — from shops in Chiado or Baixa.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Chiado or Bairro Alto — choose a restaurant that encapsulates your Lisbon food journey. Splurge slightly for your last night on a memorable meal of grilled fish, presunto (cured ham), and a bottle of Alentejo red wine. Toast to a wonderful trip.

meals.breakfast: A proper sit-down breakfast at a Lisbon café — scrambled eggs, toast, fresh orange juice, and a bica (espresso) at Café A Brasileira in Chiado, a historic literary café (€8–12).
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Tile Museum or back in Baixa — a fresh soup and sandwich at a local café (€8–12).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Chiado — try Alma (modern Portuguese cuisine, Michelin-starred, splurge option at €60–80pp) or the more mid-range Cantinho do Avillez for creative Portuguese dishes at €35–45 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure flight is in the evening. Tram 28E is a tourist favorite — ride it early in the afternoon to avoid peak crowds and pickpockets; keep belongings secure. The Tile Museum is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays — Wednesday is ideal.

Browse high-end boutiques and absorb the atmosphere of Lisbon's most refined streets. Visit the historic Livraria Bertrand, the world's oldest operating bookshop, and enjoy a slow afternoon getting acquainted with the city.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or a light welcome spread at the hotel upon arrival
meals.lunch: Upon arrival, enjoy a refined Portuguese lunch at Cervejaria Ramiro — an iconic Lisbon seafood institution known for its jumbo prawns, clams, and grilled lobster
meals.dinner: Dinner included as part of the Fado show experience at a traditional Fado house in Alfama, featuring classic Portuguese dishes such as bacalhau à brás and caldo verde paired with regional wines

day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the iconic Tower of Belém standing sentinel on the Tagus River — another jewel of Manueline architecture. Afterward, make the essential pilgrimage to Pastéis de Belém, the legendary bakery that has been producing the original custard tarts (pastéis de nata) since 1837. Enjoy them warm, dusted with cinnamon, straight from the oven. Stroll along the Tagus riverfront promenade and visit the Monument to the Discoveries.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center and enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar such as TOPO Chiado or Park Bar, offering panoramic views over Lisbon's terracotta rooftops and the Tagus. Follow with a refined dinner at one of Lisbon's celebrated fine-dining restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Sumptuous breakfast at the hotel — fresh pastries, regional cheeses, charcuterie, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Solar dos Presuntos near Belém or a riverside restaurant along the Tagus waterfront — enjoy grilled sea bass (robalo), percebes (barnacles), and local Alentejo wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at Belcanto — Lisbon's two-Michelin-star restaurant by Chef José Avillez, offering a tasting menu that reimagines classic Portuguese cuisine with contemporary artistry (reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Belém is approximately 6 km from the city center — arrange a private car or take the scenic tram 15E. Book Belcanto weeks in advance. The Jerónimos Monastery is closed on Mondays, so Saturday is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a relaxed hotel breakfast. Then head to the LX Factory Sunday Market — Lisbon's most vibrant and creative weekly market held inside a beautifully repurposed 19th-century industrial complex in Alcântara. Browse stalls selling artisan crafts, vintage items, local design, books, and gourmet food products. The atmosphere on Sundays is electric and quintessentially Lisbon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the culinary afternoon at the Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour — a premium guided tasting experience through Portugal's most celebrated food hall, sampling the finest Portuguese cuisine including fresh seafood, petiscos (Portuguese tapas), artisan cheeses, charcuterie, and traditional sweets. Meet the chefs behind the counters and learn the stories of each dish.
day_by_day.evening: Wind down with a private sunset Tagus River cruise (arrange through the hotel concierge) aboard a traditional wooden vessel, enjoying chilled Vinho Verde and local cheeses as the city glows golden at dusk. Conclude the evening with a sophisticated dinner in the Príncipe Real neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — take your time before heading out
meals.lunch: Grazing lunch as part of the Time Out Market Food Tour — multiple tastings of Portuguese specialties including grilled octopus, salt cod croquettes, bifanas, and pastel de nata
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tasca do Chico or Pharmácia Restaurant — intimate, character-rich venues serving elevated traditional Portuguese fare with exceptional wine lists

day_by_day.notes: LX Factory Sunday Market runs from approximately 10:00–19:00 and is at its best in the late morning. The Time Out Market is a short walk away. Book the river cruise through the hotel concierge for a fully private, premium experience.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Sintra Royal Palaces Day Trip — depart early by private chauffeured vehicle (recommended over the train for a luxury experience) to the enchanting UNESCO World Heritage town of Sintra, just 40 minutes from Lisbon. Begin with the fantastical Pena Palace, a Romanticist castle perched atop a forested peak with vivid yellow and red facades, offering sweeping views across the Serra de Sintra and out to the Atlantic. Explore the palace interiors and royal gardens with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the medieval Moorish Castle for dramatic hilltop views, then descend to visit the elegant National Palace of Sintra in the town center — recognizable by its twin conical chimneys. Browse the charming village streets and artisan shops. Optional visit to the mysterious Quinta da Regaleira with its iconic Initiation Well.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lisbon by private transfer in time for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a quiet, indulgent dinner in the Avenida da Liberdade area — Lisbon's most prestigious boulevard.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure to Sintra
meals.lunch: Lunch at Incomum by Luis Santos in Sintra — a refined restaurant housed in a historic building serving creative Portuguese cuisine using local Sintra ingredients including queijadas (traditional cheese pastries)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Eleven Restaurant — a Michelin-starred establishment with floor-to-ceiling views over Parque Eduardo VII, offering a sophisticated tasting menu with impeccable Portuguese wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Sintra can be crowded — departing early (by 09:00) ensures you reach Pena Palace before the main crowds. A private guide for Sintra is highly recommended and can be arranged through the hotel. Wear comfortable footwear as the terrain involves significant uphill walking.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lisbon — enjoy a long, leisurely farewell breakfast at the hotel. Take a gentle stroll through the elegant Príncipe Real neighborhood, visiting the weekend antique market (if still running Tuesday) and the beautiful Jardim do Príncipe Real. Browse the upscale concept stores and gourmet delis along Rua da Escola Politécnica for last-minute premium Portuguese souvenirs: artisan ceramics, aged Douro wines, fine cork goods, and specialty conservas (tinned fish).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museu Nacional do Azulejo (National Tile Museum) — a world-class museum dedicated to Portugal's iconic azulejo tile tradition, housed in a stunning 16th-century convent. The collection spans five centuries of decorative tile art and includes a breathtaking 23-meter panoramic tile panel of pre-earthquake Lisbon. A perfect final cultural immersion into Portuguese history and artistry.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a premier Lisbon restaurant, celebrating the end of a remarkable journey through Portugal's capital. Return to the hotel for final packing and rest before departure.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final breakfast at the hotel — order à la carte and savor every bite
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at Taberna da Rua das Flores — a beloved Lisbon tasca serving beautifully curated petiscos and natural wines in a warm, rustic setting
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Alma by Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa (Michelin-starred) — a celebration of the finest Portuguese ingredients reimagined through a modern lens, with an exceptional wine cellar featuring rare Douro and Alentejo vintages

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange luggage storage if your departure flight is in the evening. The Azulejo Museum is best visited in the afternoon when morning crowds thin. Keep the evening relaxed to allow time for final packing. Arrange airport transfer through the hotel concierge for a seamless premium departure.
